themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park-related noise complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 6.29)—suggesting either a new recurring event, inadequate enforcement, or emerging community conflict at a specific park location.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
700% spike with z-score of 6.29 (high statistical significance)
Corresponds with warming weather and possible increased park usage or unregulated activity
reporting_angles: Which specific park(s) are generating complaints and why—permitted events, youth gatherings, sound systems, or something else?
Interview Parks Department about enforcement response and community board awareness of the spike

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK from a 0.9 weekly average—a 357% spike (z-score: 5.21)—indicating possible infrastructure damage from recent weather, heavy vehicle use, or deferred maintenance now manifesting visibly.
evidence: 4 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (8-week baseline)
357% spike with z-score of 5.21 (high statistical significance)
Aligns with recurring community board budget request for street light and street infrastructure repair
reporting_angles: Map the 4 complaints to identify if damage is clustered on specific streets or widespread
Check DOT inspection data and DOB permit filings to see if recent work or paving projects are responsible

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints hit 4 three weeks ago compared to 0.1 weekly average—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72, highest severity)—though complaint volume appears to have stabilized; indicates either a removal campaign succeeded or initial wave has plateaued, but deserves clarification on what triggered the outbreak.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
3100% spike with z-score of 11.72 (highest statistical significance in dataset)
Current week data not provided; timing suggests spike may have been addressed or run its course
reporting_angles: What was being posted and where—was this a coordinated campaign, gang-related marking, or commercial advertisement?
Did DSNY or enforcement agencies respond, and what was the removal timeline?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Trend
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints rose to 14 LAST WEEK from a 4.4 weekly average—a 220% increase (z-score: 3.85)—pointing to cumulative damage from weather, tree roots, or construction activity now becoming a visible mobility hazard.
evidence: 14 sidewalk condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
220% spike with z-score of 3.85 (high statistical significance)
Part of broader street infrastructure theme (curb condition also spiking this week)
reporting_angles: Are complaints clustered on specific corridors or distributed throughout the district?
Cross-reference with DOB permits for underground work or utility repairs that may have damaged sidewalk integrity

themes_detail.label: Commercial Waste Disposal Issues
themes_detail.summary: Commercial disposal complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK from a 1.0 weekly average—a 300% increase (z-score: 4.24)—suggesting either new large commercial operations opening without proper waste management systems or enforcement gaps at existing businesses.
evidence: 4 commercial disposal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (8-week baseline)
300% spike with z-score of 4.24 (high statistical significance)
287 DOB alteration permits filed in past 90 days suggest active commercial/retail activity that may not have matched waste infrastructure
reporting_angles: Identify which businesses are generating complaints and whether they are newly opened or recently expanded
Interview DSNY and Sanitation Enforcement about whether commercial waste routes or pickup schedules have kept pace with new activity
